display.purpose: Hero identity; mobile overrides documented in DESIGN.md.

body.purpose: Recurring 14px project and architecture body text.

label.purpose: Mono controls, links, and state metadata; smaller metadata is not a reusable legibility floor.

motion.name: robot-cinematic-arrival
motion.value: 1.8s GSAP camera and rig arrival; .9s eye wake
motion.purpose: Overlaps the outgoing network intro with a three-quarter camera move; skipping resolves to the final pose. Studio reflections are generated once at 64px.

motion.name: greetly-device-breakdown
motion.purpose: Separates device layers before connecting an event to an illustrative record. Direct six-stage selection remains available. No pinning below 1100px width or 760px height, on touch or with reduced motion.

motion.name: pointer-responsive-surfaces
motion.purpose: Large images and passport tilt with cursor-positioned reflected light; headings react and key CTAs move magnetically. Fine pointers only; reset on exit and clean up for reduced motion.

motion.name: robot-gaze
motion.value: Damped head, torso and pupil tracking; 220ms blink every 4.2s while visible
motion.purpose: Original 3D robot replaces the hero compute core. Demand rendering settles between interactions; static robot remains for touch, reduced motion and GPU failure.

motion.name: homepage-entry-sequence
motion.purpose: Fullscreen SVG network converges toward the hero core; mobile has its own node composition. Skip/Escape, reduced motion, deep links and client return navigation bypass it. No live network telemetry is implied.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: System preference or stored user setting
motion.purpose: Suppress CSS motion, GSAP effects, cursor annotations, and WebGL enhancement; system preference takes priority.

rendering.lite: Width <760px or coarse pointer; static topology. Reduced motion independently disables WebGL.
rendering.balanced: Fine pointer, width 760–1199px; DPR 1, antialias false.
rendering.high: Fine pointer, width >=1200px; DPR [1,1.5], antialias true.
rendering.loading: Dynamic canvas after intersection within 180px; SVG stays visible until ready.
rendering.failure: Error boundary and WebGL context-loss handling retain fallback.
rendering.scheduling: On-demand frames in observer range; frameloop never outside it.

accessibility.focus: 2px solid var(--signal-primary), outline-offset 6px; command input uses emerald focus-within border.
accessibility.navigation: Skip link, semantic landmarks, labelled native dialog, mobile disclosure, keyboard-operable tabs.
accessibility.content: Architecture panel and complete DOM transcript stay available; decorative scene aria-hidden.
accessibility.limits: Source-grounded inventory, not blanket accessibility certification. Existing 6–9px metadata and text glyph ornaments are not canonized.

extensions.tonalRampNote: Derived OKLCH ramps are panel visualization metadata only, not additional shipped CSS tokens.

narrative.overview:
Graphite spreads, warm off-white type, and emerald signals connect a human identity to technical architecture. The recurring node, line, and signal motif gives the portfolio a coherent diagram language. Large typography and asymmetric image placement establish hierarchy; flat surfaces and thin rules keep the interface precise.

This record describes the implementation in `src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/responsive.css`, the shared layout, and its navigation, journey, capability, and scene components. The chosen world comes from `DIRECTION.md`; source-backed claims, original portrait use, and accessible alternatives follow `PRODUCT.md`. Spatial media enriches the page without owning its information.
keyCharacteristics: Architectural display type paired with restrained monospace controls.
Dark tonal surfaces, thin rules, square nodes, and sparse emerald emphasis.
Editorial asymmetry with readable DOM architecture alongside spatial media.
Native scrolling and responsive, motion-aware rendering.

rules.name: The Signal Has Meaning Rule
rules.body: Emerald identifies an action, current state, focus, or a node in the system; preserve that relationship when extending the interface.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Use Space Grotesk for human narrative and headings; use IBM Plex Mono for technical controls, state, and compact metadata.

rules.name: The Native Journey Rule
rules.body: Keep native scrolling, direct node selection, and the complete text transcript available; spatial rendering must not gate the story.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Keep content surfaces flat; reserve soft shadows for the existing overlay roles.

dos: **Do** use emerald for actions, state, focus, and meaningful network markers.
**Do** pair Space Grotesk narrative with IBM Plex Mono technical controls.
**Do** preserve thin rules, rectilinear surfaces, and varied editorial compositions.
**Do** keep keyboard selection, native scrolling, reduced motion, and DOM architecture available.
**Do** label conceptual diagrams, future work, and self-reported credentials honestly.
donts: **Don't** replace the chosen graphite/emerald world with decorative glass or generic glowing cards.
**Don't** require WebGL, animation, or pointer movement to read project evidence.
**Don't** invent proof, verification badges, performance metrics, or missing resume downloads.
**Don't** canonize the existing 6–9px metadata, repeated eyebrow labels, or text glyph ornaments as requirements for new surfaces.
